clue.text: Bug home to cover religious order

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of, covering, the second

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a sect is a religious group or order

explanation.surface: A pest has got into a monastery's house and is covering it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is everyday speech for a small creepy-crawly with six legs.

clue.text: Have no effect on unions rising in case of emergency

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the words on and unions are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of trade unions
ICE is the abbreviation for In Case of Emergency, used for a phone contact

explanation.surface: Strikes by unions in an emergency fail to make an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ON + TUC into CUTNO. TUC, Britain's Trades Union Congress, stands for the unions; ICE is the label for an emergency contact stored in a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut no ice is an idiom for failing to impress or make any difference.

clue.text: Slow boat unloaded in river

indicators.note: the emptied boat goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

indicators.note: unloaded means emptied, so only the outside letters of boat remain

explanation.surface: A slow boat with its cargo taken off sits on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, dim in understanding.

clue.text: Clears leader of Unionville, NC to cut trees all over the south

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece above lies over the one below
leader of points to the opening letter of Unionville

parts.note: NC is taken as written, the abbreviation for North Carolina
a log is a piece of cut-down tree
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A town in North Carolina is felling trees all over the southern states.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclog a pipe or drain is to free it of a blockage, clearing it.

clue.text: Make a priest or old monk take one in

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so one goes into the monk's title
completes the phrase take in, meaning admit within

parts.note: Dan is an old title of respect given to monks
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A bishop is asked to ordain a priest or let an old monk join.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... in' puts I inside DAN to make DAIN. Dan is an archaic honorific for a monk, like Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to confer holy orders, turning a candidate into a priest.

clue.text: Father John, perhaps an alternative minister

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
St John is one example of a saint, abbreviated ST
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Father John, a Catholic priest, or another clergyman could do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father John' pretends to be one priest; it is PA plus a saint's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a Christian minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Money received in report by corrupt priest?

indicators.note: in report means as heard spoken, so the sound of the words is what counts

parts.note: income is money received
bent is slang for corrupt or crooked

explanation.surface: A newspaper report claims a corrupt priest has been taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in report' tells you INCOME is spoken, giving INCUM. The question mark marks priest as an example: an incumbent holds a parish.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England a vicar or rector holding a benefice is called its incumbent, a priest by example.

clue.text: Religious instruction accepted by distant monk

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the instruction sits within the word for distant

parts.note: far means distant
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A monk in a far-off monastery receives religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a mendicant order, loosely called a monk.

clue.text: Boatman saved from abuse in holy order, shockingly

indicators.note: order as a verb means to arrange, so these letters are rearranged
saved from means taken away out of the word abuse

parts.note: an AB, an able-bodied seaman, is a boatman; Boatman is also the setter's own name

explanation.surface: The setter was rescued from mistreatment inside a religious order, shockingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saved from' removes AB from abuse, leaving USE; 'order' rearranges USE + IN + HOLY. Boatman is the setter's pseudonym, and AB is an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinously means in a wicked, outrageous manner, so in a way that shocks.

clue.text: Minister, right sort at heart, one who accepts the whip?

indicators.note: at heart means in the middle, so these go inside the minister

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church
a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: A minister who is a decent sort deep down submits to discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The whip is the party official who enforces voting discipline in Parliament, so 'accepts the whip' is about politics, not punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal party member obeys the whips' instructions on how to vote, hence the cryptic hint and question mark.

clue.text: Cleric rejecting company of cleric

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing out, so company is dropped from the word

parts.note: a deacon is a cleric ranking below a priest

explanation.surface: One clergyman refuses to keep company with another.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior clergyman heading a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Corrupt priest often seen with Candy

indicators.note: corrupt as a verb means to spoil or alter, so the letters of priest are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked clergyman is often spotted with a woman called Candy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candy' looks like a woman's name; it is the candy in candy stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy stripe is a pattern of alternating colours, so the bands of colour are often paired with that word.

clue.text: They follow the harvest, less abundant in source of comic operas

indicators.note: the word for less abundant goes inside the source's abbreviation

parts.note: G and S, Gilbert and Sullivan, wrote the Savoy comic operas
leaner means sparser, less abundant

explanation.surface: After a thin harvest, people turn to Gilbert and Sullivan for comic relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan were the Victorian partners behind comic operas such as The Mikado.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaners gather leftover grain from fields after the reapers have passed.

clue.text: Regularly in retreat? It's common now

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of retreat

explanation.surface: Is going on a religious retreat a common thing these days?
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the present calendar period, so the present age is a common one.

clue.text: Take action against head of abbey as prior goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing means these letters disappear from the longer word

parts.note: a superior is the head of a religious house
prior is taken as written, here a monk ranking below an abbot

explanation.surface: Legal action is taken against an abbot after the prior vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of abbey' looks like a first-letter pick but means a superior.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take legal action against someone in court.

clue.text: One doubts God is involved in robbery

parts.note: to be at something is to be busy with or engaged in it
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A sceptic about God is implicated in a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist disbelieves in any deity, so naturally doubts there is one.

clue.text: Mature household, female only?

indicators.note: a household for females only has had its men removed

parts.note: a menage is a household

explanation.surface: A grown-up household made up of women only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female only?' takes MEN out of MENAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older and mature, as wine or cheese does.

clue.text: Nude photo taken

indicators.note: nude means stripped, so photo loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone has taken a naked picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot goods are stolen ones, so taken in the sense of pinched.

clue.text: Cunning head of abbey concealed butcher

indicators.note: the word for cunning conceals, holds inside, the letter from abbey

parts.note: sly means cunning

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of abbey

explanation.surface: A sly abbot hid a butcher in the abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to kill them brutally, to slay them.

clue.text: Revive cannibal's victim, as Spooner might 'ave said

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the starts of words, so the opening sound moves

parts.note: a cannibal might say a man I
the cannibal's victim is a man I ate

explanation.surface: Bring back a cannibal's meal, as Spooner might have put it.
explanation.walkthrough: The victim is 'a man I ate'; shifting the M from MAN onto ATE gives AN I MATE. The dropped H in 'ave plays along with the shifted sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate is to bring to life, so to revive.

clue.text: Minister starting heretical actions in cloisters

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of Minister
heretical means deviating from doctrine, so the letters of actions are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minister begins heretical acts inside a monastery's cloisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life is lived in a monastery, enclosed within cloisters.

clue.text: Play sports here, on the right parson's place

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on the second

parts.note: the rec is British slang for a recreation ground, a public sports field
Tory means the political right, a Conservative

explanation.surface: Games are played here, on the right side of the vicar's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The rec is British slang for a recreation ground, a local playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Revealed by priest: I'm a tease of dubious value

indicators.note: Revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A flirtatious priest confesses he is a tease, a doubtful asset.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is only a rough guess, so the value it gives is uncertain.

clue.text: Reprobate changing second name to George (Boy George?)

indicators.note: changing means swapping one letter for another in the word for reprobate

parts.note: a sinner is a reprobate
N is the abbreviation for name; it replaces the second N
G is George's initial

explanation.surface: A rogue changes his middle name to George.
explanation.walkthrough: Boy George, lead of Culture Club, is the example the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy George is a well-known pop vocalist, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Call signs cause damage within Daesh

indicators.note: the word for cause damage goes inside the other group's abbreviation

parts.note: Daesh is another name for the terrorist group IS, Islamic State
to dent is to damage

explanation.surface: Radio call signs are disrupted inside the terrorist group.
explanation.definitionFit: Idents are short broadcast logos or jingles that identify a station, like call signs.

clue.text: Reject primate — that's just for starters

parts.note: to can is slang for to discard or reject
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A rejected ape is told this is merely the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small appetiser served before a meal, just for starters.

clue.text: Wash up under care of one of same 14 or 16

indicators.note: in a down answer the reversed piece comes under the other

parts.note: c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word for wash is read from the bottom

parts.note: to lave is a literary word for to wash

explanation.surface: Washing up is left to the care of a contemporary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to two other answers, ERA and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coeval is someone of the same era or age, a contemporary.

clue.text: See 10
Broken-hearted nun at bottom

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so the letters of hearted nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartbroken nun has hit rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken-hearted' looks like one word; Broken is the signal and hearted is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath means at the bottom of or below something.

clue.text: Free to neutralise leader fleeing in disgrace

indicators.note: in disgrace means fallen into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the leader, the first letter of neutralise, runs off

explanation.surface: Free to neutralise a disgraced leader who has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader fleeing' removes N from neutralise; 'in disgrace' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: At leisure means having free time, not busy.

clue.text: See 27
Neighbour to plough for us around mid-afternoon or after morning in

indicators.note: the word or comes after the morning piece
us goes around the letter taken from afternoon
mid means the middle letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone tilling a neighbour's field mid-afternoon, or after a morning inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Plough is the British name for the Big Dipper in Ursa Major, beside the Little Bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Little Bear constellation lies next to the Great Bear, which contains the Plough.
